title: Response contracts — personal scratchpad for predictable outputs
content:
Quick notepad — framing a feature I keep sketching in meetings: 'response contracts'.

Summary / motivation:
- Problem: app teams need predictable model outputs for production UX (length, format, safety, hallucination rate, style). Right now they approximate with prompt engineering + evals + heuristics. Hard to reason about programmatically, onboard new teammates, or enforce across routes.
- Idea: let developers declare a lightweight contract for a route/model combo (e.g., {format: json-schema, max_tokens: 120, style: formal, hallucination_tolerance: low, cost_bucket: econ}) and have Redwood enforce/validate at inference time + surface violations in Console + tie to rollout/rollback.
- Outcome: fewer UX regressions, easier A/Bing of safeguards, observability for contract-level SLOs. Also improves operator confidence for Dedicated/Private customers.

Hypothesis:
- If we provide a small declarative DSL for desired properties + automatic post-response validators (and cheap re-generation/fallback flows), teams will see fewer downstream errors and faster debugging when models change.

Primary personas:
- Product engineer building an assistant: wants consistent JSON output for ingestion.
- Integrations/platform engineer: needs incidents reduced from unpredictable model outputs.
- Solutions engineer: wants a safe default surface to show enterprise customers.

Rough feature components (rough PRD outline):
1) Contract spec (developer-facing)
   - JSON/YAML spec attached to a route or model-pair. Fields (initial):
     - output_shape (json-schema or enum),
     - max_tokens (numeric),
     - style_hint (string enum: concise/formal/friendly),
     - allow_external_calls (bool),
     - hallucination_threshold (float: % allowed),
     - fallback_policy (enum: regenerate/shorten/route-to-lower-temp/abstain).
   - Lightweight syntax so teams can copy-paste. Keep default for unspecified fields.

2) Runtime enforcement & hooks
   - Pre-send: attach contract metadata in request routing.
   - Post-response: run a validator pipeline (fast checks: JSON parse, schema validate, token count, simple hallucination heuristics like unsupported-entities).
   - If violation: apply fallback policy. Options:
     - Auto-regenerate with stronger system instruction + stricter temperature.
     - Trim and patch (if shape has optional fields, fill with placeholders and mark partial=true).
     - Route to a safe-model variant (smaller, deterministic) or to a fallback text generator that responds with an apologetic abstain/retry message.

3) Console surface
   - Per-route contract editor with quick presets ("strict ingestion", "loosened creative", "safety-first").
   - Live metrics: contract pass rate, avg tokens on pass/fail, rollback events.
   - Links to failing example payloads + quick one-click re-run in sandbox.

4) Observability & SLOs
   - Allow teams to set contract-level SLO (e.g., 98% pass rate). Generate alerts when trending down.
   - Integrate with existing rollouts: canary evaluation collects contract pass rate before full rollout.

5) Evals + CI integration
   - A small test harness: given a prompt set and expected contract, compute pass/fail and surface diffs for regressions. Plug into CI (e.g., on model update) to prevent bad rollouts.

6) Pricing/Cost considerations
   - Contract enforcement may cause additional calls (regenerations). Provide a toggle to allow "best-effort" vs "enforced (may cost more)". Show estimated extra token cost in console before enabling.

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I want the assistant to return valid JSON matching schema X 99% of the time so my downstream parser doesn't crash.
- As an SRE, I want to trigger an alert when contract pass rate drops below 95% so I can investigate model drift.
- As a platform engineer, I want the ability to route failed-contract requests to a non-LLM fallback so we can provide a consistent degraded UX.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: create/update/delete contract attached to a route.
- Runtime: post-response validator that checks JSON schema + token count + parses boolean flags. On failure, run a single regenerate attempt using a deterministic template.
- Console: show last 50 contract failures with payloads and a toggle to enable/disable enforcement per-route.
- Evals: a simple CLI tool that reads a small prompt/test-set + contract and reports pass rate.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Keep validation synchronous but bounded (e.g., one regeneration attempt) to avoid latency blowups. Provide async mode for background correction and user notification.
- Heuristics for hallucination detection will be lossy. Start with entity-checks and unknown-claims heuristics (compare responses to provided "source set" when present).
- Storage: contract could be stored as route metadata (works for hosted + dedicated + private). For private customers, ensure contract definitions integrate with their policies and KMS (no secrets in contract file).

Experiments to run (early lab):
- Pick two internal routes (one ingestion-focused, one conversational). Define strict vs loose contract. Run model updates (e.g., baseline -> quantized variant) and measure pass rate delta.
- Cost tradeoff experiment: measure extra token overhead for regenerate fallback vs percent improvement in pass rate.
- UX experiment: show failure examples in the Console to two groups of engineers: one with current logs-only, one with contract-failure dashboard — measure time-to-debug.

Open questions / risks:
- How to specify hallucination_threshold in a way that is actionable? Need a good lightweight scoring function.
- Fallback semantics for multi-turn contexts — regenerating might break session continuity. Maybe allow "context-aware retry" vs fresh response.
- Could enforcement create a perverse optimization where models learn to output minimal-but-bizarre content that passes the validator? Need diverse evaluators.
- Latency & cost: how do we surface expected cost and make it obvious to engineers?

Console UX rough ideas (brainstorm):
- Contract presets carousel with short descriptions and expected token multiplier.
- Inline "preview" that runs a sample prompt through contract and shows result.
- Contract diff view when a model update changes pass rate (list failing examples).

Next steps / TODOs (for me / small follow-ups):
- [ ] Draft minimal contract schema (start with output_shape, max_tokens, fallback_policy, enforce: bool).
- [ ] Prototype a post-response validator in sandbox that checks json-schema + one regeneration attempt.
- [ ] Run internal experiment on /assistant/generate route with baseline 13B model. Capture pass rate baseline. (Ping Miles to pair on data collection.)
- [ ] Sketch Console wireframe + validation toggle (pair with Priya for product wording).

Notes to self: keep this small and composable. Start with a single, clear enforcement for JSON output — that buys a lot of value for integrations. Focus on observable signals that non-ML folks can act on (failing payloads, pass rates) rather than deep ML-only metrics.

Slack threads / refs: #platform-policies, #hosted-api-product, jira JIRA-API-1124 (linked above).

---
Personal brainstorming style: deliberately messy. If this looks useful, next doc could be a one-pager spec + a tiny API sketch (POST /routes/:id/contract).
